scope.evidence: H1 'Build a Career Quiz That Matches Interests to Fields of Work' and meta title 'Take a Free Career Quiz or Build Your Own' cover the whole job; hero description 'Build a career quiz that sorts interests into fields of work and keeps every result in a database you own. Try the sample below.' leads with Build and carries the primary; how-to description is one sentence.

intent.evidence: AMBER SERP of issuer-run free quizzes: the page carries a playable eight-question quiz ('Career Quiz: Which Field of Work Fits You?') with six field-of-work results, plus the build angle for counselors, colleges, coaches and workforce boards.

specificity.evidence: 'his result screen lists the three trade electives tagged for that field: welding, construction, and auto technology'; 'a salary floor of $64,000'; 'Of the 640 visitors who finished, 190 landed on Helping and Teaching'.

openers.evidence: Feature bodies open on full sentences: 'Name the fields of work, programs, or jobs you want as results.'; 'Each finished quiz becomes a row in a database you own'.

craft.evidence: QC Q2/Q5/Q7 clean; short declaratives such as 'Write it down before the first question.' No blocking craft defect.

voice.evidence: Plain product verbs: 'Emergent builds the questions with each option pointing at one result, and changes any of them by prompt.' One voice note on the meta description.

truth.evidence: claims_used all approved (free-start, api-connect, alerts, no-caps, custom-domain, code-export, database-owned); 'The O*NET Interest Profiler ... measures six types of occupational interests' matches the quoted onetcenter.org span; 'asks eight questions and names one of six fields' matches spec.quiz (8 questions, 6 results); 'Free' in the meta title is true of the on-page quiz and of the approved free-start claim; tab 4 bars 190+170+120+160 = 640.

distinct.evidence: Own story set (Fenwick Lake juniors, Cedar Plains divisions, coach Simone Lacroix, Tallowford job fair); sibling primaries appear only as FAQ link anchors ('style quiz', 'vocabulary quiz').

faq.evidence: 10 written items, each answer-first ('Yes. Emergent is free to start...'); hub link in item 2; links to style, vocabulary and free-trial pages; paa --spec 10 pass, 0 reject, 0 flag; no brands or file formats in questions.

images.evidence: Contact sheet: tab 1 'Your result: Building and Fixing' with Welding, Construction, Auto technology and 'Email to Joanna Venter'; tab 2 'If the result is Health Sciences -> Calvin Rudd', '3 certificate programs shown'; tab 3 'Salary floor $64,000', Logistics analyst and Inventory planner; tab 4 640 finished, Helping 190, Building 170. One hero per panel, all agree with the tab copy.

findings.quote: Take a free career quiz that names the field of work your interests point to, then build one for your students or job seekers. Free to start.
findings.issue: 'free' twice in one 141-character snippet; the closing fragment reads tacked on.
findings.fix: Keep one 'free', for example end on '...for your students or job seekers.'

findings.quote: Good ones ask about tasks and settings, not job titles.
findings.issue: Restates howto_step_3 'Ask about tasks, not job titles' and FAQ 1 'asks about the tasks and settings you enjoy'.
findings.fix: Let FAQ 8 lean on a different test, such as whether the result names a next step.

findings.quote: It should show the field the answers lean toward, three jobs in that field, and one next step
findings.issue: Same idea as howto_step_5_des 'Then name three jobs and one next step' and FAQ 8 'it should name jobs to explore and a next step'.
findings.fix: Vary one of the three mentions.
